subject: Renewal: SLA upgrade & capacity plan for Horizon Commerce
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@horizoncommerce.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal conversation: SLA & capacity needs

Hi Grace,

Our renewal is up in June and the product team has flagged two blocking items before we can sign the new term:

1) A formal latency SLO for inference (we're asking for p95 <= 600ms for typical 2k token prompts across our peak region).
2) A commit increase — we need an additional 40% headroom on our Dedicated pool to cover a big feature launch in Q3 (estimated +4 A100-equivalent GPUs, or an equivalent throughput bump).

We currently average ~10M generation tokens / month and have occasional bursts that saturate our pool. Procurement is also asking about support tier changes — they want a documented escalation path and a 24/7 premium support option (response SLA for Sev1 incidents). Attached is a short usage snapshot for Q1.

Can your team share options (SLA language, pricing delta for premium support, and a timeline to provision the extra capacity)? If we can get something reasonable, Horizon is ready to commit to a 12‑month renewal with a modest expansion.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Park
Head of Platform
Horizon Commerce
elena.park@horizoncommerce.com
Attachments: Horizon_Q1-usage.pdf (report)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizoncommerce.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: SLA & capacity needs

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the data. Quick acknowledgement and a couple of clarifying items before we put formal options on paper:

- For the latency SLO: is the 600ms p95 target measured from your edge to the single-token latency, or do you mean end-to-end generation for an average 2k-token response? (These imply different provisioning patterns.)
- For capacity: when you say +4 A100-equivalent GPUs, is that a sustained increase or expected to be required only during a 6–8 week launch window?
- Support: can you share who your primary on-call / escalation contact will be (prod owner + procurement contact)? Procurement is listed as procure@horizoncommerce.com.

Preliminarily, we typically offer two upgrade packages at renewal: (A) dedicated capacity bump + standard SLA uplift, and (B) premium SLA (faster response, guaranteed p95 latency, credits on breach) + priority escalation + 24/7 support. Option B usually requires an operations onboarding (2 weeks) and a minor increase to committed spend (~20–30% uplift depending on capacity). I'll loop Marcus (sales lead) and Ava (solutions engineer) to scope provisioning impact and put together SOW language.

Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to align? I can share a draft SOW and SLA options on the call.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai; ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-03T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: SLA & capacity needs (internal)

Internal notes (please keep internal):

- Margin / pricing guardrails: for an account this size (10M tokens/mo baseline), target net uplift should be ~25% on committed spend for premium SLA + capacity. If they take the capacity for only a 6–8 week window, structure as a temporary burst commitment (extra reserved nodes billed prorata) — avoids long-term overcommit.
- Engineering: Ava, assess whether we can meet p95 <= 600ms for 2k prompts in us-east with an extra 4 A100 equiv. If not, propose a p95 for 1k and a different p95 for 2k with increased dedicated KV cache.
- Legal/Sales ops: prepare two SOW attachments — (1) capacity bump + standard SLA, (2) premium SLA with credits (0.5% revenue credit per hour of qualified downtime beyond SLA up to max).

Attachments: SLA-options-2026.pdf (internal template).

Marcus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@horizoncommerce.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai; ava_chen@redwood.ai; Horizon Commerce Procurement <procure@horizoncommerce.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: SLA & capacity needs

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a concise proposal with two concrete options:

Option 1 — Capacity Boost (short-term / prorated):
- Increase Dedicated pool by 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for a 12-week window starting on agreed go-live.
- Standard support (business hours) and 99.5% uptime commitment.
- Pricing: prorated on extra reserved nodes; no change to base SLA.

Option 2 — Premium SLA + Priority Support (recommended for launch):
- Guaranteed latency SLOs: p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 600ms for 1k prompts; p95 for 2k prompts defined as an operational target with measured baseline and a 30% uplift in reserved throughput.
- 24/7 premium support with 1-hour initial response for Sev1 and named escalation path.
- Financial remedy: service credits for qualified breaches (methodology in appendix).
- Requires 2-week ops onboarding and a 30% uplift on committed spend (estimate; final pricing to be confirmed in SOW).

Attachments: RDW_SOW_Horizon_v3.pdf (proposal & SOW draft). DocuSign link below if you'd like to sign the SOW and reserve capacity immediately: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning?doc=RDW_SOW_Horizon_v3

If Option 2 looks good, we can prepare the final SOW and get procurement to sign. Target provisioning lead time after signature is ~10 business days for capacity + 2 weeks for onboarding.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the appendix details.

Best,
Grace
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@horizoncommerce.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai; marcus_lin@redwood.ai; ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Horizon Commerce Procurement <procure@horizoncommerce.com>
Date: 2026-05-07T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: SLA & capacity needs

Hi Grace / Marcus,

Thanks for the clear proposal and the two options. Executive summary: Horizon prefers Option 2 (Premium SLA + Priority Support) but with two small changes before we sign:

1) Payment terms: procurement wants Net 45 instead of Net 30.
2) Latency SLO wording: request p95 <= 600ms for 1k prompts and p95 <= 900ms for 2k prompts (we will accept the 2k as an operational target if you include an explicit throughput provisioning plan in the SOW).

Procurement is ready to issue a placeholder PO (attached) once we have final SOW with the amended payment term. We'll also need the named escalation contacts included in the SOW appendix.

If you can send a final SOW with those two small edits, we can circulate and sign this week.

Elena
--
Elena Park
Head of Platform, Horizon Commerce
Attachments: Horizon_PO_5678.pdf (placeholder PO)
